description: Write-like shell operations whose target is inside a guarded layer (raw/ or wiki/). Each deny pattern is a Python regular expression matched against one pipeline segment; TARGET expands to the layer's target regex. Every layered rule must carry the TARGET token: after a segment that changes into the layer (cd_into), following segments are matched with TARGET removed, so any write there is denied, and a rule that hardcoded raw/ or wiki/ instead would be unreachable after a cd. Segments are split on unquoted separators only, so a pattern may run to the end of its segment. A cd anywhere else leaves the layer. Rules in `deny_always` carry no TARGET and are about the command itself rather than a layer, so they match everywhere and are judged before any exemption; `reason` overrides the layer's message. Read-only commands (cat, rg, grep, head, sed without -i, ls, wc, git status/log) never match. A layer's `xargs` pattern names the writers that a pipeline may not feed into it; it mirrors that layer's deny rules minus its skip_rules. Extend this list rather than the hook code.

deny_always.name: verify script
deny_always.reason: running verify.py is blocked: `verified` records that a person read the page against its sources, so only the owner runs the script. Ask the owner to run it themselves, exactly as printed, with `! python3 <plugin>/scripts/verify.py "<page>" --by <id>`.

raw.reason: {rule} targeting raw/ is blocked: raw/ is the immutable source layer. Read it freely (cat, rg, head, sed -n). To add a source use /agent-wiki:fetch; to change one, ask the owner.

wiki.reason: {rule} targeting wiki/ is blocked: pages are written with the Write and Edit tools or the plugin scripts, so the verified and sources guards can check the result. Deleting or moving a whole page (rm, mv, rename.py) stays allowed.
